headline: Prairie Trails and Lakeside Horizons
reservation: State parks like Cedar Hill and Dinosaur Valley often require day-pass reservations through the Texas Parks and Wildlife website. These can sell out weeks in advance for holiday weekends; check official portals before arrival to ensure entry.

days.title: Lakeside Sun and Skyline

stops.name: White Rock Lake
stops.detail: Cycle the 9-mile loop or paddle the calm waters with a view of the Dallas skyline.

stops.name: Dallas Arboretum and Botanical Garden
stops.detail: Stroll through 66 acres of seasonal floral displays overlooking the lake.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes; urban surface streets can be busy.
days.note: Motorized boats are restricted on White Rock Lake, ensuring a quiet environment.

days.title: Escarpment Hikes and Western History

stops.name: Cedar Ridge Preserve
stops.detail: Trek through cedar forests and up limestone bluffs for views of Joe Pool Lake.

stops.name: Fort Worth Stockyards
stops.detail: Experience the open-air cattle drive and explore the historic district's wooden boardwalks.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; traffic between Dallas and Fort Worth is frequent.
days.note: Cedar Ridge trails are often closed after heavy rain to prevent erosion; check the official status.

days.title: River Bottoms and Nature Refuges

stops.name: Fort Worth Nature Center and Refuge
stops.detail: Walk the marsh boardwalks and view the resident bison herd in a native prairie setting.

stops.name: Trinity River Audubon Center
stops.detail: Explore trails through hardwood forests and wetlands along the Trinity River.

days.driving: Allow 1-1.5 hours; these sites are on opposite sides of the Metroplex.
days.note: Early morning is the best time for wildlife sightings like bobcats and migratory birds.

intel.title: Lakeside Lot Limits
intel.text: White Rock Lake parking lots can fill by 10 AM on sunny Saturdays. The Dallas Arboretum requires pre-paid parking reservations during major festival months.

intel.title: Metroplex Coverage
intel.text: Strong 5G coverage is standard across Dallas and Fort Worth. Expect slightly weaker signals in the low-lying areas of the Trinity River bottomlands.

intel.title: Urban Infrastructure
intel.text: Gas and EV charging are abundant in Grapevine and Plano. Ensure your vehicle is ready before heading to the more remote sections of Ray Roberts Lake.

intel.title: Heat Awareness
intel.text: Summer temperatures often exceed 100 degrees; plan strenuous outdoor activity before 9 AM. Spring bluebonnet season typically peaks in early April.

intel.title: Trail Conditions
intel.text: Cedar Ridge Preserve features natural surface trails with significant steps. The Katy Trail in Dallas is a flat, paved multi-use corridor accessible to all.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at DAL or DFW; transit to Downtown Dallas or Fort Worth. Stop in Grapevine for water and trail supplies.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are ideal; RVs should check bridge clearances in historic districts and state park hookup availability.
plan.goldenHour: Cedar Ridge Preserve overlooks for sunset; check seasonal park closing times which vary.
